Area.evidence_source: Half the prisoners (23/46, 50%) stated that they had not received any type of support or therapeutic intervention following their suicide attempt: I felt really vulnerable. I was promised ...there was all this mention of 'you will be seeing a mental health person so that they can follow up how you're feeling' and I've had nothing. I've gone numerous times and said I need to talk to someone and they are just like 'I will get an SO [Senior Officer]' or 'I will get this person or that person' and then you hear nothing. It's just the same thing day in, day out ...the same thing. I've experienced that since I've been in here. One person passes it on to another person and you just wait in your cell for hours and you are just left there waiting, thinking someone is going to come and no one comes. And that is frustrating. That is just a buildup and you end up getting angry and frustrated. The most common support reported as being offered was someone to talk to (15/ 46, 33%): They were good staff. They would come in and have a chat with me all the time. They would come into my cell and sit down and they would have a cup of tea and they would chat to me all day. Someone to talk to ...I felt a bit better. If I talk about it sometimes then it's a bit better instead of bottling it all up.
